previous_assumption: assumed the Requirement detail page's Request quotation link (navigating to /quotations?requirementId=...) actually did something for the Renter who clicks it
correction: It was a complete no-op for a Renter: CreateQuotationDialog (what that requirementId query param is meant to open) only renders when organizationType === rental_company -- Renters cannot create quotations at all (quotation.manage is rental_company-only). The button's entire premise was navigating the wrong party to a screen only the other party can use, and never notified anyone. Real fix: added QuotationResponseService.requestQuotation (rfq.manage, Renter-only; requires the target company's own response to exist and be interested, ConflictError otherwise) which notifies that specific Rental Company with a new requirement.quotation_requested notification type. Deliberately NOT wrapped in the swallow-notification-failures try/catch every other notify() caller in this codebase uses -- those already did their real DB write and the notification is a side effect; here notifying IS the entire business action, so a failure must surface to the caller rather than silently returning success having done nothing. Also: the notification needed its own relatedResourceType (quotation_request, not requirement) since /requirements/[id] is Renter-only and the recipient here is a Rental Company -- reusing requirement as the resource type would have sent them to a page they cannot access. Worth checking whether other frontend action links that navigate to a query-param-driven flow (the ?xId= pattern used across auctions/quotations/billing) actually work for BOTH organization types that might click them, not just the one the original author had in mind.
